body:
Follow-up from #440 / PR #472. The invoice page's UTC day is fixed, but the same class of bug remains across the readers that format a **stored business day**:

- `transfer-history-page.tsx`, `location-transfer-history.tsx`, `outbound-transfers-page.tsx`, `debt-ledger-panel.tsx` — a bare `toLocaleDateString()` renders the day in the **machine's** timezone, so a UTC or non-Algerian machine shows the wrong day.
- `salaries-section.tsx`, `consolidation-dialog.tsx`, `record-entry-payment-dialog.tsx`, `void-entry-dialog.tsx`, `employee-details-page.tsx` — `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("ar-DZ")` without a `timeZone`, same problem.
- `license-settings.tsx`, `home-view-derived-formatters.ts` — optioned formatters missing `timeZone`.
- `settings-section.tsx` — an update-check timestamp with `toLocaleString()` (fixed in the #461 branch that this issue replaces; re-apply).

## Task

1. Add one pinned helper for a stored business day and use it everywhere; where a formatter takes options, pass `timeZone: getAlgeriaTimeZone()`.
2. **Add a hygiene rule**: production web source may not call `toLocaleDateString(` or `new Intl.DateTimeFormat(` without a `timeZone` in the same balanced call. Self-test the rule against a pinned and an unpinned sample plus a comment mention, so it cannot pass vacuously.
3. TZ-pinned tests for each screen: render under `TZ=UTC` and assert the Algeria day. Each must fail on the pre-fix source.
4. The "current month" quick filter for the expenses bar, with the KPI label following the filter (all-time wording when no date filter is applied, period wording when one is). A filter still opens empty; the toggle makes a period one click away.

## Why it was not fixed in #472

The original branch carried this sweep, and it was lost to a conflicted rebase against that branch's own successors (#463/#464/#468 rewrote the same files). Re-applying it is a substantial change of its own — ten readers, a hygiene rule and a new filter control — not a fix to the invoice day, and the design-pass rule is explicit that a finding whose fix would sprawl belongs in its own issue with the finding attached.

A test that renders under a non-Algerian timezone is the guard: without one, every one of these sites looks correct on the machine it was written on.
title: Pin every stored business day to Africa/Algiers, and forbid a bare date formatter
